title: A3.ApplicationComponent
description: A modular, deployable part of an application

id.description: the instance's permanent key — the source tool's own persistent id

x-sdem-source.locator: schema/level-model.schema.json › instance.id; identity rules in docs/knowledge-graph-spec.md §4

id.x-sdem-reasoning: Every relationship points at it; it must be unique in its level and never reused (knowledge-graph spec KG-I-01).

type.description: an entity type from the catalogue
type.x-sdem-reasoning: Ties the instance to the Architecture Metamodel; must be concrete and of the export's level.

version.x-sdem-reasoning: Relationship ends pin it, so an approved relationship refers to a known state.

x-sdem-source.locator: schema/level-model.schema.json › instance.name; identity rules in docs/knowledge-graph-spec.md §4

name.x-sdem-reasoning: Shown in traces; a rename changes the name, never the id.

lifecycle_status.x-sdem-reasoning: Lets retired things stay referable and planned (design) things be marked as such in traces.

canonical_id.description: external reference id, e.g. a BIAN concept id on A2 instances

x-sdem-source.locator: A2 end of BIAN-authority relationships; required before approval — schema/relationship-registry.schema.json

canonical_id.x-sdem-reasoning: BIAN-authority relationships require it on the A2 end before approval.

description.x-sdem-reasoning: Read by the step-5 text rule for capabilities and domains.

definition_uri.x-sdem-reasoning: Points to the institution's or the standard's definition.

source_id.description: the record's key in the tool it came from

x-sdem-source.standard: Dublin Core (DCMI Metadata Terms, DCMI Recommendation 2020-01-20)

source_id.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Which record in the source tool is this? The record's own key in the tool it came from, so any node can be traced back to its system of record. Distinct from SDEM `id`, which may be the same value.

created.description: date it was created in the source

x-sdem-source.standard: Dublin Core (DCMI Metadata Terms, DCMI Recommendation 2020-01-20)

created.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: How old is this? Date the thing was created in the source.

modified.description: date it was last changed in the source

x-sdem-source.standard: Dublin Core (DCMI Metadata Terms, DCMI Recommendation 2020-01-20)

modified.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: What changed recently? Is this stale? Date of the last change in the source; lets reviews spot stale entries.

x-sdem-source.standard: Dublin Core (DCMI Metadata Terms, DCMI Recommendation 2020-01-20)

valid_from.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Is this in force on a given date? Start of the validity period. Dublin Core defines `valid` as a date or range; SDEM stores the range as two dates.

valid_to.description: date it stops being in force (empty = open-ended)

x-sdem-source.standard: Dublin Core (DCMI Metadata Terms, DCMI Recommendation 2020-01-20)

valid_to.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Is this in force on a given date? End of the validity period (empty = open).

replaces.description: the earlier instance this one supersedes

x-sdem-source.standard: Dublin Core (DCMI Metadata Terms, DCMI Recommendation 2020-01-20)

replaces.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: What did this replace? The earlier instance this one supersedes, so history can be followed through renames and re-designs.

replaced_by.description: the later instance that supersedes this one

x-sdem-source.standard: Dublin Core (DCMI Metadata Terms, DCMI Recommendation 2020-01-20)

replaced_by.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: What replaced this? The later instance that supersedes this one.

conforms_to.description: standards, frameworks or policies it follows (e.g. "BIAN BCM 14.0")

x-sdem-source.standard: Dublin Core (DCMI Metadata Terms, DCMI Recommendation 2020-01-20)

conforms_to.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Which standard, framework or policy does this follow? E.g. "BIAN BCM 14.0", an internal policy id. Makes alignment claims explicit and queryable.

x-sdem-source.standard: Dublin Core (DCMI Metadata Terms, DCMI Recommendation 2020-01-20)

subject.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Find everything about a topic (e.g. "payments", "fraud"). Free topic tags; lets architects slice the graph by theme.

owner.description: the actor or role accountable for it

x-sdem-source.standard: ArchiMate 3.2 concept (confirmed via the Archi oracle; specification text login-gated)
x-sdem-source.locator: assignment (active structure assigned to behaviour or object)

owner.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Who is accountable for this? Accountability is the most-asked design question. No public standard defines an "owner" field: Dublin Core's rightsHolder is about rights, not accountability. Built on ArchiMate's assignment of an actor or role.

access_classification.description: how sensitive it is and who may see it

x-sdem-source.standard: Dublin Core (DCMI Metadata Terms, DCMI Recommendation 2020-01-20)

access_classification.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Who may see this? How sensitive is it? Dublin Core defines the field (access or security status); the four values are SDEM's common banking scale, not a standard.

deployed_on.description: ids of the A4 platforms that host it

x-sdem-source.locator: assignment (node assigned to deployed artifact), ch. 10

deployed_on.x-sdem-reasoning: The join key for DEPLOYED_ON. ArchiMate expresses hosting as a node assigned to the deployed artifact; SDEM records the platform on the component.

x-sdem-source.locator: SDEM join key for DEPLOYED_AS (rule S32) to the SDEM Deployment entity — docs/architecture-entity-design.md

deployed_as.x-sdem-reasoning: The join key for DEPLOYED_AS, pointing at SDEM's Deployment entity.

built_as.description: ids of the A4 artifacts it is built as
built_as.x-sdem-reasoning: ArchiMate: an artifact realizes an application component; SDEM records the artifacts on the component.

network_zone.description: id of the A4 network it sits in

x-sdem-source.locator: SDEM join key for rule S37; zone-wins precedence from use case C3 finding 3 — docs/use-case-testing.md

network_zone.x-sdem-reasoning: No standard field; SDEM's convenience key for S37. A network's connects list is the alternative; the zone wins when they disagree (C3 finding).

vendor.description: the supplier of the component ("in-house" when built by the bank)
vendor.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Who supplies this application? Same meaning as CycloneDX supplier; name kept so existing exports stay valid (A3 data-model review, 2026-10-25).

accesses.x-sdem-reasoning: Duplicates the within-level access relationship already in the export; one example carries it. Deprecated: use the relationship.

release_version.description: the product release that is in use (not the version of this model record)
release_version.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Which release of the product are we running? CycloneDX names the version of a component exactly this way; checked 2026-10-24. Distinct from the core `version`, which versions the architecture record.

license.description: the licence, as an SPDX identifier (e.g. Apache-2.0)
license.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Which licences do we depend on, and are any restricted? SPDX identifiers are the public standard for naming licences and CycloneDX uses them; checked 2026-10-24.

cpe.description: the product's CPE 2.3 name, for vulnerability matching
cpe.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Which published vulnerabilities affect this application? NIST's standard product naming, used to match vulnerability records; checked 2026-10-24.

x-sdem-source.standard: NIST SP 800-145 The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing (public)
x-sdem-source.locator: service models SaaS, PaaS, IaaS (§2, PDF p.6–7)

hosting_model.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: What runs on premises and what runs in the cloud? NIST defines the three cloud service models; checked 2026-10-24. SDEM adds `on-premises` for applications outside any cloud, so the value list is SDEM's.

recovery_time_objective.description: how quickly the application must be back after an outage (e.g. "4h")
recovery_time_objective.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: How fast must this application recover? Defined in NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (NIST glossary); checked 2026-10-24. The resilience measure banks report, more precise than a criticality label.

recovery_point_objective.description: how much data loss is tolerable, as a time (e.g. "15m")
recovery_point_objective.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: How much data can this application afford to lose? Defined in NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 (NIST glossary); checked 2026-10-24.

disposition.description: what the bank plans to do with the application
disposition.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Which applications do we keep, invest in, replace or retire? The application-rationalisation question. Published classifications are proprietary, so SDEM defines its own plain values.

attributes.x-sdem-note: undefined attributes are allowed here but reported as warnings by sdem-graph check

x-sdem-entity.reasoning: ArchiMate 3.2 Application Component, ch. 9 — concept present in the open-source Archi implementation of the ArchiMate 3.2 relationship tables (commit 9e6a014), which the relationships test looked up; specification text is login-gated.
